_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Come to me, says Jesus, all who are weary.
We are tired, and we have come.
Take my yoke; it is easy, and the burden is light.
We will learn the gentleness of God.
What the wise overlooked, you showed to children.
Teach us, and we will rest in you.
Come, let us worship the God who carries us.
We come for rest. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Feel the weight come off your shoulders for an hour — the yoke set down, the load you carried in laid at the door.
Come to me, and I will give you rest.
You came in tired: the week, the worry, the burdens too heavy to name out loud.
Come to me, and I will give you rest.
Jesus does not hand you a heavier load; he offers his own yoke, gentle and easy, made to fit.
Come to me, and I will give you rest.
What the clever could not grasp, God reveals to the weary and the small — so come as you are, and breathe.
Come to me, and I will give you rest. Thanks be to God!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: You came in carrying more than you can name.
Come to me, and I will give you rest.
Set down the load; the yoke he offers is gentle.
Come to me, and I will give you rest.
What the wise missed, God shows to the weary.
Come to me, and I will give you rest.
Come, let us worship the God who carries us.
Come to me, and I will give you rest. Amen.
